summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic venous insufficiency, lipodermatosclerosis, prosthetic heart valve, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for nausea, chills, and abdominal pain. She was found to have Group B streptococcal bacteremia, likely originating from her chronic leg skin changes. She was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and vancomycin initially, then transitioned to amoxicillin after pathogen identification. Her symptoms resolved, and she completed four days of IV antibiotics before discharge. She was prescribed a 10-day course of oral amoxicillin to complete treatment. An echocardiogram showed no valvular infection. Her INR was subtherapeutic, prompting a warfarin dose adjustment. She improved clinically and was discharged home with follow-up arranged.
problems: Streptococcus, group B, as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
